The core operators—Levy processes, Malliavin derivative, and stochastic integral—are foundational in modeling discontinuous dynamics. Their interplay underpins both probabilistic inference and system evolution. The stochastic integral allows integration against jump processes, while the Malliavin derivative provides sensitivity analysis. These structures form a dual framework where the former governs evolution and the latter enables reverse-engineering of probabilities. Failure occurs when jump intensities exceed regularity constraints or when functionals lack differentiability. The Kunita-Watanabe inequality ensures boundedness of stochastic products, crucial for convergence in GSE simulations.
